news.title: CAF Strategy Conference: Carlos Queiroz – five World Cups and a Ghana campaign with lessons for Africa
news.lede: Carlos Queiroz will arrive at the CAF Strategy Conference in Cabo Verde only days after his spell as Ghana coach came to an end, but carrying with him another chapter in one of international football’s most travelled coaching careers. The 73-year-old mutually ended his agreement with the Ghana Football Association on 1 October, just weeks after being handed a new mandate following the FIFA World Cup 2026. Despite leaving the Black Stars, Queiroz will still attend the Conference in Sal to share the experience of guiding Ghana through one of the most demanding groups at the World Cup and into the knockout stage for the first time since 2010.

news.title: AFC Nations League explained: What it means for India's World Cup dream
news.lede: Asia’s road to the FIFA World Cup could look very different from 2030, with the Asian Football Confederation proposing a biennial Nations League that would bring World Cup and Asian Cup qualification into a single, more structured system. For India, that could mean more meaningful football, but it could also make the climb towards the World Cup a tougher one.According to draft plans seen by ESPN, the AFC is proposing a three-tier Nations League involving all 47 member associations, with 18 teams in each of the top two tiers and 11 in the third. The first official edition is proposed for 2030, while a pilot competition in 2028-29 would help decide where teams sit when the new system gets underway.The real significance of the proposal will be felt when the Nations League is linked to the World Cup.

news.title: Messi readies for final farewell in Argentina send-off
news.lede: Lionel Messi will bring the curtain down on his glittering Argentina career on Tuesday (Bangladesh time Wednesday) with a farewell friendly against Benin that marks the dawn of a new era for the South American champions. After more than two decades of service to his country, the 39-year-old superstar will hand over the captain's armband for good as he makes his final appearance in the Albiceleste jersey at the Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires. Messi will be joined for his international swansong by 85,000 spectators and several of the teammates with whom he reached the pinnacle of football at the 2022 World Cup in Qatar, alongside members of Argentina's emerging generation. . Who will captain Argentina after Messi?
